title: Audit log enrichment pipeline for vuln alerts and RBAC tagging
summary: Working proposal for an enrichment pipeline that augments raw scanner/SCA outputs and platform audit logs with RBAC-context tags and normalized evidence fields before SIEM export. Goal is to make vuln alerts actionable for triage, automated patch routing, and audit evidence ingestion without adding friction to oncall flows.
goals: 1) Attach RBAC ownership and environment tags to vuln signals. 2) Normalize evidence payloads (code paths, package coordinates, proof artifacts) into a compact schema for SIEM. 3) Provide deterministic fields that reduce false positives in automated patch assignment. 4) Allow downstream teams (SRE, infra, platform) to filter by ownership and SLA.
background: We ingest multiple vuln sources (dependabot/OSS scanners, internal infra scanner, container image scanner, SCA as a service). Each emits different schemas and varying levels of context. SIEM dashboards and automated runbooks need consistent keys: asset_id, ownership, environment, vuln_id, severity_score, evidence_refs, and remediation_state. RBAC v2 rollout requires we tag events with role and team ownership so playbooks can auto-route. This doc outlines an incremental enrichment pipeline and the minimal audit schema changes needed for adoption.
scope: This proposal covers the enrichment layer (service that subscribes to scanner webhooks and platform audit stream), the minimal audit-log schema additions, SIEM export mapping, and a phased rollout. It excludes changes to scanner detection logic and the full RBAC policy engine (only requires queryable ownership metadata).
proposed_schema_changes: Add the following normalized fields to enriched events before SIEM export: 'asset_id' (string), 'asset_type' (host/container/artifact), 'team_owner' (string), 'owner_role' (string, e.g., service-owner/platform-owner), 'environment' (prod/staging/dev), 'vuln_tracker_id' (string combination of source:id), 'cvss_score' (string/float), 'evidence_refs' (array of short refs), 'first_seen' (ISO date), 'remediation_status' (triage/in_progress/fixed/mitigated/ignored), 'sla_days' (integer), 'priority_bucket' (P0-P3). Also propose 'rbac_tag_version' to indicate which ownership mapping was applied.
enrichment_steps: 1) Intake: normalizer reads scanner payload + platform audit log for the same time window.
2) Resolve asset canonical id via inventory service (call: /inventory/resolve).
3) Fetch ownership metadata from RBAC v2 lookup (fast cache, TTL 5m).
4) Compute priority_bucket using cvss + deployment_criticality + age-of-vuln heuristics.
5) Attach evidence_refs (s3 keys / ticket links) and compress large proof blobs into evidence digest.
6) Emit 'enriched_vuln_event' to SIEM export topic and to our vuln-tracker kafka topic for downstream automation.
7) Persist a minimal JSON blob (for audit) to evidence-store with retention metadata for compliance.
alert_routing_mapping: Mapping rules (initial): if owner_role == 'service-owner' then route to PagerDuty escalation policy 'service-pager'. If priority_bucket == 'P0' and environment == 'prod' also create high-priority SIEM case and page SRE. For infra-owned assets (owner_role == 'platform-owner'), route to 'platform-oncall' and tag ticket with 'auto-assign:true' to enable automated remediation playbook. Tickets created should include evidence_refs and RBAC tag + rbac_tag_version.
siem_export_notes: Export format: flattened JSON, max 64KB per event. Do not include raw stack traces; include evidence_refs only. Map fields to Splunk indexes: idx=vuln_enriched (asset_type, team_owner, priority_bucket). Also produce a compact CSV line to the legacy SOC pipeline for backward compatibility. Include rbac_tag_version and enrichment_pipeline_version in every export for auditing. If enrichment fails, emit a 'vuln_enriched_failed' event with error_code and raw_ids so we can retry.
privacy_and_compliance: Ensure evidence blobs stored in evidence-store are encrypted with customer KMS where required. Audit-log additions must not leak PII. For private deployments customers, enrichment must run in-customer VPC by default; provide a connector mode. Retention defaults: enriched metadata 2 years, evidence content 365 days, configurable by enterprise contract.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (2 weeks): build enrichment lambda + test on non-prod scanners. Phase 1 (4 weeks): opt-in beta for one internal product team, route enriched events to a test SIEM index. Phase 2 (6 weeks): enable for all prod scanners with a 24-hour dark-liverun where we publish enriched events to a non-alerting index to validate. Phase 3: enable auto-ticketing and remediation playbooks. Rollback knob: 'enrichment_enabled' per-scanner via feature flags (LaunchDarkly).
operational_metrics: Key metrics: enrichment_success_rate, avg_enrichment_latency_ms, avg_rbac_lookup_ms, percent_events_with_owner, false_positive_reduction_estimate (baseline vs enriched). Dashboards should show per-scanner breakdown and top teams receiving routed tickets.
open_questions: 1) What is the canonical inventory identifier for images vs hosts? inventory currently returns 'asset_key' or 'host_id' inconsistently.
2) Should we include temporary 'triage_hint' freeform field for human notes? (privacy concerns)
3) How do we handle ownership for cross-cutting infra features that have no single team-owner?
4) SLA calculation: use calendar days or business days for external vendors?
